research: Mengxin Zheng is an assistant professor of computer science at the University of Central Florida. Her research focuses on machine learning security and cybersecurity, with particular interest in backdoor attacks and defenses, AI data privacy protection, and the robustness of large language models. Zheng earned a doctorate in computer engineering from Indiana University Bloomington in 2023. She has served on program committees for conferences and journals in her field. Her work has been recognized with several awards, including a Young Fellow designation and a best student paper award

name: Qian Lou

research: Qian "Ken" Lou is an assistant professor at the UCF Department of Computer Science and a member of the UCF Cyber Security and Privacy Cluster. Before coming to UCF, Lou was a senior research scientist at the Samsung Research AI center. He obtained his master's and doctoral degrees from Indiana University Bloomington in 2019 and 2021, respectively. Lou won the Luddy Outstanding Research Award and a best paper nomination at the prestigious ACM PACT conference. His research interests include deep learning, e.g., CV and NLP model compression, privacy-preserving/secure machine learning, and computer architecture, e.g., hardware accelerators.

He is also actively engaged in interdisciplinary areas including demand-side management, distribution system optimization, and the energy-water-food nexus.

Her research has been published in leading journals and conferences in the field of quantum computing, including Quantum, Quantum Science and Technology, IEEE Transactions on Quantum Engineering, DAC, ICCAD and DATE. She is a member of the Berkeley Quantum Synthesis Toolkit, or BQSKit team, contributing to a powerful open-source framework for quantum compilation, with more than 100,000 downloads.

His group develops saltwater electrodes, seawater electrolyzers and related electrochemical platforms that enable carbon-negative hydrogen production, scalable CO2 removal and resource recovery from complex aqueous streams. He also advances high-throughput electrochemical characterization methods to accelerate the discovery of catalysts and functional materials, and to study corrosion mechanisms and materials degradation in nuclear environments.
